newsitem.title: UK: Dunblane spells end for UK swim clubs' pistols.
newsitem.headline: Dunblane spells end for UK swim clubs' pistols.

text.p: British swimming clubs plan to phase out starting pistols in the wake of the Dunblane massacre, which led to a ban on most handguns, The Times reported in its Saturday edition.
It said swimming officials had decided that the use of starting pistols was inappropriate.

"We're not saying they're necessarily dangerous, but in the current climate we ask whether children really need to see guns at the poolside. We think not," David Sparkes, secretary of the Amateur Swimming Federation of Great Britain, told The Times.
Sparkes estimates that swimming clubs hold about 2,000 starting pistols, which fire blanks.

"They are a potential hazard and there are dangers of guns being stolen and used in robberies and so on. We believe we are acting responsibly in drawing up a plan to phase out starting pistols," he said.
An experiment using klaxons to start races at this week's British championships was unsatisfactory and Sparkes is hoping an inventor will come up with an alternative.

The government banned all handguns above .22 calibre following the Dunblane massacre in March, when lone gunman Thomas Hamilton entered the Scottish town's primary school and killed 16 young children and their teacher.
